title: The `is_unsafe` substring gate hard-refuses legitimate in-corpus approval questions, and it is documented nowhere in the graded docs
section: 3. Retrieval, prompting, citations & guardrails / 4. Agent orchestration
why_it_costs_marks: Band 5 asks for "correct, cited, grounded responses" and "excellent guardrails". This is the only confirmed defect in the whole set that is a product behaviour rather than prose, and the only one the project's own disclosure discipline skipped: the structurally identical bare-balance rule gets a design-doc paragraph plus Known limitation 14, while this one appears in no graded document, has no negative test for the false-refusal class, and is not covered by the run's over_refusal_rate 0.000 (n=18) because no dataset item contains a listed phrase. It also carries live demo risk: an improvised question during the recording can hit it.
evidence: `.venv/bin/python -c "from hrmosaic.agent.router import is_unsafe; ..."` returns True for "What happens if I submit a request without manager approval?", "Can I take PTO without manager approval if my manager is on leave?", "Is there any way to skip the manager step when they are on holiday?" and "Who can approve my own expense report?", and False for "What is the policy on self-approval?" — the intent the gate exists for. src/hrmosaic/agent/router.py:172-175 is a bare substring scan over 21 phrases; src/hrmosaic/agent/orchestrator.py:1236 calls it unconditionally on the raw message, before out_of_scope and clarify, returning `_refuse_unsafe` with outcome="refused". The manager-on-leave case is answerable from corpus/manager-approval-matrix.md:141-172 (delegation rules). `grep -rIn 'is_unsafe|UNSAFE_PHRASES|_refuse_unsafe' README.md design-and-evaluation.md docs/requirements-traceability.md docs/demo-script.md` returns nothing.
fix: Cheapest and highest-value: disclose it, which converts it from an undisclosed defect into the same bounded limitation class as the bare-balance rule — add a row to design-and-evaluation.md's safety section and a Known-limitations entry stating the 21-phrase breadth, the bound (adds a refusal only, fails closed, cites the matrix, redirects to People Ops, no tools/call, no write) and the fix. The code fix (gate on intent=='action' or a first-person request verb, or exclude negated forms) plus a negative test with the three phrasings above is the right answer but touches src/, which breaks the empty-diff provenance contract five documents print and forces a re-drive of the published run and both ablation arms.
effort: 15 min to disclose; ~1 h of code plus a full re-drive (~3 drives, $1.30-2.70) to fix properly

title: The evaluation segment tells the presenter to walk two metric tiles the run-detail page does not render
why_it_costs_marks: docs/demo-script.md:85 is the one segment carrying the rubric's evaluation walkthrough, and two of the eight figures it names are not on the page it sends the presenter to. Worse, under that page's own **Workflow completion** heading the presenter would be saying 0.933 while the screen shows the per-workflow pills 66.7% and 50.0%. Falsifiable with a single GET, and the script elsewhere warns the presenter not to read figures off the Runs page where both figures actually live.
evidence: The live run-detail page's strip is `headline_metrics + ('clarification_accuracy',)` (src/hrmosaic/web/templates/dashboard/eval_detail.html:66) over the eight keys in src/hrmosaic/web/dashboard.py:182-190, which exclude doc_recall_mean and workflow_completion (:220-221 labels them "the two the compare tab charts"). Python regex over the fetched page: `97.4` → 0 hits, `93\.3` → 0 hits, "Documents recalled" → 0 hits. Both figures are on /dashboard/evals and the Compare chart, which the same segment reaches seconds later.
fix: Rewrite the tile-walk sentence to name the nine tiles actually on the strip, and move "document recall 0.974" and "workflow completion 0.933" into the Compare-tab beat at the end of the same segment where both are charted. One sentence, no code change.

title: design-and-evaluation.md names 34d50fb as "the build that is deployed" in the present tense, which one curl refutes
why_it_costs_marks: Two present-tense sentences in the primary graded document are false at HEAD, and they are the two a grader falsifies first — the provenance check is the obvious thing to try. README.md and deployed.md both carry the correct hedge ("the live sha moves; the application tree does not"); the design document does not, and it never prints the pathspec that would let a reader reconcile the two shas in place.
evidence: `curl -s https://mosaic-hr-copilot.onrender.com/health` → app.git_sha 204d48fd6104e53e9b526c37ab751f8086d93e2d = HEAD, against design-and-evaluation.md:20 "live service on commit `34d50fb` — the build that is deployed" and :1504 "its `target_git_sha` equals the deployed sha". The substance holds: `git diff --stat 34d50fb..HEAD -- src mcp/tools corpus data/index/chunks.manifest.jsonl Dockerfile render.yaml requirements.txt` printed nothing (exit 0).
fix: Reword both to "the build the application tree at HEAD still is — the live `/health` sha moves with every documentation deploy; see the pathspec command in `deployed.md`" and link deployed.md's provenance paragraph, so the sentences survive the next docs push.

title: Three sentences point at "the provenance pathspec this document prints" in a document that prints no command
why_it_costs_marks: A dangling self-reference in the primary graded document, three times, one of them ("the pathspec above") with no antecedent in either direction — line 604 is the file's first use of the word while the only provenance discussion is at 1053, below it. Tests/contract/test_published_run_commands.py pins five documents as printing the command identically and design-and-evaluation.md is deliberately not one of them, so "this document prints" is false by the project's own construction.
evidence: `grep -n 'this document prints\|pathspec above' design-and-evaluation.md` → 604, 1053, 1991; `grep -c 'git diff' design-and-evaluation.md` → 0. The five documents that do print it are README.md, deployed.md, docs/pre-submission-checklist.md, docs/requirements-traceability.md and CHANGELOG.md.
fix: Either print the pathspec once in the deployment-choices section and add design-and-evaluation.md to the contract test's document list, or reword all three to "the frozen provenance pathspec `deployed.md` prints" with a link.

title: "28 of them open mid-word" overstates a measured 23 in three live places
why_it_costs_marks: A quantified claim in the graded design document that one script falsifies. 28 is the number of continuation windows whose first character is lowercase; 23 are preceded by a non-whitespace character and so genuinely open inside a word, because src/hrmosaic/rag/chunk.py:148-151 lstrips a window that starts on whitespace. The earlier regrade had it right at 23; the a57ed44 fix pass introduced the conflation while fixing the surrounding sentence.
evidence: Grouping data/index/chunks.manifest.jsonl by (doc_id, heading_path): continuations 29, lowercase-first 28, preceded-by-non-space 23. Six continuations are preceded by a space or newline (e.g. ' ' → 'nominates an onboarding b', '\n' → 'specific work, not genera'). Live at design-and-evaluation.md:241-243, :2170 and .env.example:56.
fix: Change the three live sentences to "28 open with a lowercase word and 23 open inside a word", and keep the measuring snippet beside the figure so the next edit re-derives it.

title: Five source comments and the architecture page claim a decline emits a *second* confirmation span; the code resolves the pending one in place
why_it_costs_marks: docs/architecture.html:1649 asserts the exact inverse of the implementation ("a second confirmation span is emitted, never an in-place update of the pending one") in a reader-facing §10 artifact, and web/api.py:1831 contradicts a comment 56 lines below it in the same function. None of these five sites is among the four stale comments Known limitation 15 discloses, so a grader grepping for the second span finds a contradiction the docs have not accounted for — and the limitation list's own stated criterion ("contradicted by a live document or test") is met by all of them.
evidence: `grep -n add_span src/hrmosaic/web/api.py` → one hit, line 1518, and it writes an `error` span. The only confirmation-span writer in src/ is Orchestrator._propose (orchestrator.py:3007-3019, user_response="pending"); decline_turn → _resolve_proposal → core/trace.py:947-970 `resolve_confirmation`, self-described as "The only UPDATE to `spans` in the codebase". Stale sites: src/hrmosaic/web/api.py:1831, src/hrmosaic/core/trace.py:111 and :886, docs/architecture.html:1647 and :1649. Contradicted in place by api.py:1887-1889.
fix: Correct docs/architecture.html:1647/1649 now (it is outside the frozen pathspec), and add api.py:1831 and trace.py:111/886 to the limitation-15 list with their corrections until the next application rebuild.

title: mcp/README.md and architecture.html say the per-turn tool array is "OpenAI-shaped"; the deployed provider is Anthropic
why_it_costs_marks: R5.5 requires documenting how the agent client discovers and calls tools, and the Discovery flow is that artifact. The shape claim is false for the shipped path — render.yaml:23 sets LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic, and AnthropicAdapter._tool_payload emits {name, description, input_schema} with no OpenAI envelope. mcp/README.md also contradicts its own step 2, which already names AnthropicAdapter as the thing that shapes the wire, and design-and-evaluation.md:400 states it correctly, so the MCP documents disagree.
evidence: mcp/README.md:83 "converted to OpenAI-shaped function schemas"; docs/architecture.html:1534 "the live catalog becomes the OpenAI-shaped tools array every turn" and :1625 the same. src/hrmosaic/core/llm/anthropic.py:274-284 returns {name, description, input_schema}; the `{"type": "function"}` envelope exists only in openai_compat.py:200-201, an adapter the deployed service does not select.
fix: Reword all three to "converted per turn to the provider's own tool shape — Anthropic-shaped by `AnthropicAdapter`, which is the deployed path — never a hard-coded list". Leave the dated 2026-09-08 spec alone.

title: deployed.md's provenance table gives the published run a time its own stated rule contradicts

title: A cancelled write is filed as outcome `refused`, and two consequences of that are undisclosed
why_it_costs_marks: The core mislabel is disclosed as Known limitation 13 with a live capture, but two reader-facing effects are not: the a11y live region keys on outcome, so a screen-reader user who cancels their own card hears "I can't answer that one." over visible text reading "Cancelled — nothing was created."; and templates/_turn.html:151-153 asserts a declined confirmation "carries no steps … gets no library link" while `_refuse` keeps the redirect next_steps, so the policy-library link does render.

Live: docs/evidence/draft-hr-email-live-2026-09-22.txt line 111 `-- outcome: refused` with two next steps.

title: docs/evidence/README.md attributes the 390-capture count to index.json's `screen_ids`, which holds the 72 ids
why_it_costs_marks: Two errors in one parenthesis: 390 is recorded under `screen_count`, not `screen_ids`, and "72 × 3 (390 captures)" invites the reader to compute 216 with nothing explaining the extra 174. README.md's own version of the clause binds it to the 72 correctly, so the evidence index copied it onto the wrong number.
evidence: scripts/ux_capture.py:401-402 writes `"screen_ids": ids` and `"screen_count": len(self.entries)`; the live .ux-capture/index.json has len(screen_ids)=72 and screen_count=390, with the extra 174 being the `#full` full-page variants of 58 ids (per-id counts Counter({6: 58, 3: 14})). docs/evidence/README.md:90-91 carries the claim; docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/task-16-report.md:172 states it correctly.
fix: Rewrite as "**72** screen ids over 3 viewports plus the full-page `#full` variants of 58 of them — **390** captures, the `screen_count` `make ux-capture` prints beside the 72-entry `screen_ids`". Note the extras are `#full` variants only, not dark-scheme or phone-only screens.
